title: add JSONSchema strict mode + improved error reporting for OpenAI compatibility
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: we need deterministic structured outputs for high-confidence downstream tooling and OpenAI-compat clients. This PR implements a strict JSONSchema response_format mode and improves error reporting so OpenAI-compat consumers can fall back or surface actionable messages. Changes include: 1) response_format: "json_schema" now accepts a "strict" option which enforces exact schema conformance at generation time and fails fast on mismatch; 2) validation: server-side JSONSchema validator with streaming-aware partial-parse checks to avoid blocking streaming endpoints; 3) errors: canonicalized error shapes that match OpenAI compatibility expectations (error.type, error.message, error.details) and conversion layer for legacy clients; 4) SDK compatibility: small additions in the Python SDK openai compatibility shim to expose strict mode flags and improved client-side error helpers; 5) docs: updated openai_compat.md and response_format examples; 6) tests: unit + integration tests covering strict and non-strict flows, streaming token recovery, and metrics for validation failures. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged (non-strict). Strict mode must be opted-in via response_format.strict = true or via OpenAI-compat header. Performance: validator runs incrementally and uses cached compiled schemas; a microbenchmark shows ~5-10% p99 latency impact on heavy token rates when strict validation is enabled (included in PR comments). Rollout plan: feature-flag gated for 2 weeks in staging, then gradual rollout to hosted API with a prompt-shielding canary and metrics dashboard to monitor failure rates and latency. Referenced Linear tickets: ENG-5123 (schema validation streaming), PM-1289 (OpenAI compat behavior).
